FISHING LICENCE · CANADA

New Brunswick fishing licence

Visitors aged 16 and older generally need an angling licence. A salmon licence and a guide can be necessary even when a basic angling licence seems sufficient.

Official rules ↗

Updated 2026-11-11

Who needs one

  • Visiting anglers aged 16 and older.
  • Visitors targeting sea-run Atlantic salmon need the salmon licence category.

Who doesn’t

  • Visitors under 16 need no licence for fish other than Atlantic salmon.
  • An unlicensed visitor under 16 can share an accompanying salmon licence holder's catch-and-release limit.

Licence options and prices

LicenceForLengthPrice

Non-resident salmon 3-daynon resident3 consecutive days$53 CAD

Fishing with a guide or charter

Visitors need their own appropriate licence. A licensed guide is required on Guide Required Waters after the designated date, unless an exemption applies.

Rules visitors should know

  • Obtain a New Brunswick Outdoors Card number before purchase.
  • Short licences cover consecutive calendar days.
  • Check the guide requirement for the exact water and date.

How to buy

Use the Fish and Wildlife Licensing System, an authorized vendor, or Service New Brunswick.

Common license questions

Do I need a fishing licence in New Brunswick?

Visitors aged 16 and older generally need an angling licence. A salmon licence and a guide can be necessary even when a basic angling licence seems sufficient.

How much is a visitor fishing licence in New Brunswick?

Non-resident general season, except sea-run Atlantic salmon: $64 CAD; Non-resident general 7-day, except sea-run Atlantic salmon: $41 CAD; Non-resident general 3-day, except sea-run Atlantic salmon: $30 CAD; Non-resident salmon season: $173 CAD (checked November 2026).

Where do I buy a fishing licence in New Brunswick?

Use the Fish and Wildlife Licensing System, an authorized vendor, or Service New Brunswick.
